heuristics: Table walk on 6-element classes collides at least 94.3% as fast as ideal random draws (Teske 2001; van Oorschot-Wiener 1999; Brent-Pollard 1981; Duursma-Gaudry-Morain 1999)

Cycle rates follow index-coincidence counting with table indices modelled as independent uniform draws; the 2-cycle rate is charged at the strict upper bound 2^-20 (Bos et al. 2010; Bernstein-Lange-Schwabe 2011)
Per-step instruction counts and the per-DP allowance are stated bounds, not measurements; the escape re-entry bound is a random-mapping model
Low 76 bits of the canonical x are uniform up to a 2^-175 relative error (orbit-count density 3(1-t)^2); successive steps' index bits are independent as part of the walk model
limitations: Memory about 2^76.6 bytes is astronomically large and not realisable.
Per-step extra work E=830 instructions is a stated itemised upper bound (771 itemised plus a 59 reserve), not a measurement; the score holds for any true E up to 837.
The trap (escape re-enters its own cycle) bound 2^-189.1 and the cycle rates are random-mapping model bounds, not theorems.
The batched doubling escape and the cycle rules are proved for merging (section 3); only their cost is heuristic.
